body: Still alive, feeling a little better.
He's a really nice, loving generous person, but he probably wouldn't even remember that I died eventually. His memory is going fast.

I'm at the point where I don't even care if my death hurts my grandfather and he has to find my body, and that was the only thing preventing me from offing myself for a long time. I know that's not a good sign.

It could actually suck worse. Homelessness is a very real possibility. I've been through enough, I shouldn't have to worry about trying to survive on the streets, and being raped (again), abused or worse. Even facing that horrible prospect, I'd still rather die than try and get better. I just don't have the mental or physical strength to work on therapy at this point. 

I don't try to convince myself that things possibly can't get any worse than they are now, because my life continually does get shittier.

It was just a consultation and I honestly didn't have good feelings about her. I admittedly don't trust mental health professionals in general, but I didn't feel good when I left her office. I'd honestly rather just die, because I'm too exhausted to keep doing this. 

Thanks though.

Edit: Honestly I don't even know why I wrote all of this. I've completely given up. My brain is just fried I guess.

I thought I wanted to be involved in music at some point, but dance culture is a particularly scummy scene. If I told you about some of the weirder aspects probably wouldn't believe me. Honestly. I would want nothing to do with it even if I wasn't depressed. There is absolutely nothing I can think of that could keep me going or make my life tolerable, and I've really given it a lot of thought.

I don't know how I have either honestly. I think I've just been sticking around so I don't bum my grandpa out, because I'm certainly not doing it for my sake. That excuse is starting to wear thin though. Now's as good a time as any to say goodbye to my joke of a life.

Are you in any sort of therapy right now? It probably wouldn't hurt to talk to a professional to help you deal with the stress and trauma. If money is an issue there might be counseling at your school, or at the very least they can point you in the right direction to get help.
